when_to_offer: at a genuine unresolved player decision or a meaningful player-facing event handoff with multiple materially distinct lawful responses, when the player has not already declared the next action
duration_rule: Show an estimated in-world duration, narrow justified range, or qualitative scene-relative horizon when time materially affects the decision and current player-visible context supports it.
legality_gate: current tactical geometry when danger is immediate
current player-facing semantic capability when persistence is implied
horizon_rule: Horizon is relative to the scene, not a fixed clock category.
normal_scene_rule: Prefer three materially different immediate actions plus two materially different wider-horizon actions or objectives, then Free Action. Adapt the mix when the scene cannot support both horizons and never add filler merely to reach the default count.
combat_horizon_rule: In active combat or immediate danger, wider-horizon choices are tactical objectives for the next several exchanges or battle objective, such as positioning, protection, capture, escape, isolation, or disengagement. Do not offer unrelated long-term administration.
strategic_horizon_rule: In downtime, command, political, institutional, training, relationship, or planning scenes, wider-horizon choices may concern hours, days, weeks, projects, training cycles, commitments, delegation, missions, relationships, institutions, or strategy when player-visible and lawful.
interrupt_rule: If a suggestion crosses a known scheduled obligation or hard causal interrupt, state the expected boundary in player-visible terms.
information_rule: Choices may state predictable commitments and player-known tradeoffs, but may not promise success, imply a hidden best answer, reveal unseen opposition, leak unknown facts, or encode repository-only information.
premise_parity_rule: Every material premise used by a suggested choice must already exist in fresh player-visible context or the immediately preceding narration; choice text cannot create hidden terrain, actors, resources, restrictions, or opportunities.
declared_intent_rule: If the player already declared a clear action, resolve it instead of presenting a menu. If one consequential clarification is required, ask only for that clarification.
standing_continuation_rule: A declared wait, timeskip, sequential choice, or broader continuation remains unfinished turn intent until its target/horizon is reached, a genuine player-facing event or protected decision interrupts it, or the runtime makes further execution unavailable. A quiet maintenance/time chunk is never turn completion by itself.
activity_handoff_rule: scene.activity_handoff is a derived player-safe turn-completion cue, not a second authority. requires_player_decision=true is a stop boundary. continue_without_player=true may carry only an already-declared continue, standing wait, or procedural purpose through lawful runtime continuation and never authorizes a new protected Wei choice. next_boundary_at/target_time are horizons, not elapsed time. status=scene_open proves no automatic continuation by itself.
ooc_detour_rule: An OOC DEV repair, deployment check, source maintenance step, or scene repair does not consume or cancel still-unfinished IC intent. If the same player message or unresolved ordered declaration says to continue afterward, refresh live context and resume that declared intent automatically when it remains lawful.
event_seek_rule: When a declared wait/timeskip has a known horizon and an event-seeking command is available, prefer that semantic path over arbitrary short advance_time chunks. Internal causal-work chunks remain invisible and automatic until the horizon or a genuine player-facing interruption is reached.
meaningful_event_handoff_rule: After fully presenting a delivered report, briefing, interruption, reveal, arrival consequence, or other meaningful player-facing event, offer grounded response options when two or more materially distinct lawful next actions exist even if scene.decision_required is null. Do not manufacture options when the event has only one obvious procedural continuation or the player already declared that continuation.
report_handoff_rule: A report is not a choice by itself. Present its player-readable content first. If the content creates multiple materially distinct responses, show choices at that resulting fork; if the player already said to open, read, answer, or act on it, carry that declared action through before offering a new menu.
selection_render_rule: An unambiguous numbered/menu selection becomes an explicit in-world Wei action or line of dialogue within the exact scope of the selected option; never resolve it as an invisible interface click.
bounded_delegation_rule: Explicit permission to use Wei judgment/stats authorizes one bounded answer only; use relevant fresh sheet and player-visible knowledge when material, render the answer, and do not carry the delegation forward.
menu_rule: Choices are concise, nonbinding suggestions with no default or recommended option unless the player explicitly asks for advice. Any legal natural-language free-form action remains allowed, and visible options must differ in actual approach, commitment, timing, delegation, risk, information gain, resource use, or horizon rather than cosmetic wording.
storage_rule: Never cache generated choice menus in scene state.
handoff_rule: Classify endpoints as new decision, meaningful player-facing event handoff, obvious procedural continuation, standing wait/declared continuation, unavailable durable stage, or genuine completion. A null unresolved decision does not by itself end the scene or suppress useful choice scaffolding after a meaningful event.
